pages.text: $(thing)Steel Pumps$() and $(thing)Steel Pipes$() carry fluids: $(thing)Water$(), $(thing)Salt Water$(), $(thing)Spring Water$(). They move source blocks, lift them upward, which $(l:food/aqueducts)Aqueducts$() cannot do, and top up small enclosed pools.$(br2)A pump moves water, it does not make it: the block it takes leaves its source. Only a river stays as it was.

Steel pipes are forged from $(l:metalworking/steel)Steel$() on an $(l:metalworking/anvils)Anvil$(). A $(thing)Steel Pump$() is made of some pipes and $(l:getting_started/primitive_alloys#brass)Brass Mechanisms$().
A pump needs a $(l:mechanics/crankshaft)Crankshaft$() and $(l:mechanics/mechanical_power)Mechanical Power$():$(br)$(li)It joins a pipe at its $(bold)bottom$().

$(li)On its narrow side the pump stands against the working end of a crankshaft.$(li)The line of pipe is up to $(bold)16$() blocks long, and its open end must stand in the liquid. The atmosphere lifts water only about 10 m, so that end may lie no more than $(bold)10$() blocks below the pump. A deep mine needs pumps in stages.$(li)While the crank turns, liquid comes out on the wide end a block at a time.

The lift is work, and it loads the shaft: the higher the water goes, the harder the crank is to turn. A block takes tens of seconds even at the full speed of a water wheel, and a wheel that is too weak, or a lift that is too high, stops the shaft. TFC++ adds a pump of its own for pipes: see $(l:tfcpp/pipes)Pipes and Pressure$().
